answer: In an agent market trading copper, each account must lock $100 for 30 days before it can submit one bid per minute. Splitting into 1,000 identities therefore ties up $100,000; creating names alone buys no access. Even when interest rates reach their nadir, the attacker loses use of that capital for a month. The limit makes a hollow crowd of fake agents costly because bidding capacity scales with locked funds, not claimed identities.
